action: Take RDM refrigeration controllers off the public internet and apply RDM's new firmware, as Pen Test Partners advises; see RDM advisory RDM-SA-2026-001.
exec: Exposed refrigeration controllers at retailers and food sites are a risk, so operators should check whether theirs are reachable from the internet.
plain: UK agencies, retail groups and researchers worked to secure internet-exposed RDM supermarket fridge controllers; RDM released new firmware, but smaller operators may still be exposed.

key_findings: Pen Test Partners says Danfoss controllers are not particularly popular in the UK and the more popular controllers there are from RDM.
Pen Test Partners says it is not publishing exploits or the discovery method.
RDM has released new firmware, per Pen Test Partners.
recommendations: Take controllers off the public internet.

summary: Pen Test Partners says a significant vulnerability in RDM refrigeration controllers, found by Omega Solutions, led NCSC to issue an urgent alert to UK supermarkets; it calls the issue largely mitigated, though smaller cold chain operators may still be exposed. Cooling Post reports RDM released new firmware, and that Omega alerted NCSC and, with the British Retail Consortium, DEFRA and the Food Standards Agency, began contacting supermarkets.
title: UK agencies and Pen Test Partners work to secure exposed RDM supermarket refrigeration controllers

validation.note: Pen Test Partners (read in full) and Cooling Post (read 22 November) independently report the RDM controller vulnerability, NCSC's involvement, RDM's new firmware and that the issue is largely mitigated with smaller operators possibly still exposed. Security.NL relays the BBC, which could not be loaded. Merged with uk-fridges-critical-flaw-securing-race-2026-11 (LBC, Guardian via AOL).
